overview: Perran Beach starts right in Perranporth and runs north-east for about three kilometres to Ligger Point, a huge, wide expanse of sand facing west into Perran Bay. This page covers the southern end by the town; the northern part is known as Perran Sands.
Perranporth is a seaside town with shops, cafés and pubs along its main street, so this end of the beach is easy for a family day with everything close by.

expect.title: Surf and swimming
expect.text: It’s a popular surfing beach. Lifeguards patrol from May to September; swim between the flags.

expect.title: Space
expect.text: Even in summer the sheer size of the beach means you can usually walk away from the busiest part near town.

expect.title: History in the dunes
expect.text: In the dunes behind the beach, at Penhale Sands, are the remains of St Piran’s Oratory, a 7th-century chapel that lay buried under sand for centuries.

goodToKnow.label: Getting there
goodToKnow.text: Perranporth is around 11 km south-west of Newquay on the B3285, and the coast path passes along the edge of town.
